subject: fixing p parameter to zero when using occumulti()

messages.author: 4c0169060ac9f545
messages.subject: fixing p parameter to zero when using occumulti()
parts:
Hello,

I am using occumulti() to explore species pairwise co-occurrence patterns. Here, detection is a function of a survey specific categorical covariate with two levels (A and B). In the species detection histories, the first 14 occasions are using level A and the remaining 8 are using level B. For species 1, only levels A applies (the last 8 occasions have NAs in the detection history) and for the other species, both levels apply. Now, I want to fix the detection probability for level B for species 1 to zero. Otherwise, it is automatically converting B detections to NA for the other species also.  What would be the argument to fix this parameter to zero?

Thanking you for your help.

Divyajyoti

messages.author: 4f80e1927b0757cb
messages.subject: Re: fixing p parameter to zero when using occumulti()
parts:
Hi Divyajyoti,

In order for a sampling occasion to be usable by the model both species must have been sampled during that period. That's why an NA for any species on an occasion converts the rest of the samples to NA as well. So unfortunately there isn't a way to incorporate the final 8 sampling periods (and their associated covariates) into the model if species 1 was never sampled during that period.

It *may* be possible to incorporate the extra data for species 2 somehow with a custom model in e.g. BUGS, but I doubt it.

Ken
